challenges.finding: Publisher reports the Avakubi PoC (Nia-Nia, Ituri) closed for insecurity and 4 other PoCs idle over two months of late payment; the Butuhe PoC (Nord-Kivu) non-functional since a provider died on 26 September; 4 Viadana PoCs (Bas-Uele) stopped by a continuing provider strike; unpaid September salaries in Ituri and Haut-Uele and three months of arrears in Nord-Kivu; a provider strike at the Kasenyi CTE and a strike at Tchomia; a health centre burned at Lolwa (Ituri); rumours at Bafwasende including a call to burn the general hospital, where response activities remain suspended for insecurity; and Tshopo safe burials failing (10 of 10) because the order was not executed. Already printed in earlier editions: the Avakubi closure (SR173 to SR177), Butuhe closed since 26 September (SR178), the Viadana strike (SR173 to SR176), the Kasenyi CTE strike (SR173 to SR175, SR178), the Bafwasende suspension (SR171 to SR178) and Tshopo burial failures for non-execution of the order (SR178: 13 of 14); the unpaid September salaries, the Tchomia strike, the Lolwa health centre and the Bafwasende hospital rumour are new in SR179. No intervention effect is established.

Contact follow-up covers six reporting provinces. The 267-contact cohort is printed under Nord-Ubangi with values identical to the SR178 Bas-Uele row, so its province attribution is withheld. Tshopo has the lowest rate (56.1%) while Bafwasende activities remain suspended for insecurity; the page does not say whether Bafwasende contacts are included in the Tshopo count, and no zero follow-up is inferred.
